TreVeyon Henderson.note: Ruled out for the season opener after missing all game-week practices with the ankle injury suffered Aug. 24. Week 2 remains uncertain.

Zach Charbonnet.note: Unavailable for at least the first four games while rehabbing a torn ACL. Seattle has been encouraged by his rehab, but there is no firm return date.

Tory Horton.note: Was limited throughout game week and inactive for Seattle's opener. Hamstring issue follows an injury-interrupted 2025 season.

George Kittle.note: Successfully returned from the January Achilles tear in San Francisco's Week 1 win over the Rams, catching two of five targets for 12 yards with no reported in-game setback. His usage remained below a normal Kittle workload, but completing the game materially improves near-term availability confidence. Participation is expected to increase progressively in coming weeks.
George Kittle.expectedReturn: Active; workload expected to ramp up

Rome Odunze.status: Expected active Week 1 - calf; pregame confirmation pending
Rome Odunze.note: NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reports Odunze is expected to play against Carolina despite the questionable designation. That materially improves the outlook from the prior not-yet-medically-cleared status and offsets the concern created by Chicago's Saturday WR elevation. A modest workload cushion remains because Odunze was limited in all three practices and is returning from a strained right calf; official confirmation is still due with game-day inactives.
Rome Odunze.expectedReturn: Expected active Week 1; modest workload limitation possible

Jonathon Brooks.status: Cleared Week 1 - groin resolved; no limitations
Jonathon Brooks.note: Carolina removed Brooks from the final Week 1 injury report after he practiced fully Friday. Head coach Dave Canales said Brooks has no limitations entering the opener. The groin-related availability and workload penalties are removed; the residual long-term-risk modifier reflects his history of back-to-back right ACL surgeries rather than the resolved groin issue.

Zay Flowers.status: Cleared Week 1 - hamstring; off injury report
Zay Flowers.note: Flowers progressed from limited Wednesday to full participation Thursday and Friday and is no longer listed on Baltimore's final Week 1 injury report. With no game designation and a full Friday practice, the remaining short-term workload cushion is removed. A minimal long-term-risk modifier remains for the recent soft-tissue issue until regular-season game action is completed without setback.

Michael Penix Jr..note: Practiced fully, but Atlanta has confirmed Penix will be inactive for Week 1 while the team continues a cautious return-to-game ramp following his 2025 ACL tear. The full practice is encouraging, but game availability has not yet been restored.
Michael Penix Jr..expectedReturn: Week 2 or later; no firm game-return date

Tua Tagovailoa.note: Atlanta has ruled Tagovailoa out for the Week 1 opener after the oblique injury suffered during Thursday practice. He was absent from the media-access portion of Friday practice, and Cooper Rush will start against Pittsburgh. No firm return timetable beyond Week 1 has been announced, so Week 2 remains possible but uncertain.

Alvin Kamara.status: Questionable Week 1 - MCL; limited role expected if active
Alvin Kamara.note: Kamara progressed to a full Friday practice and is medically cleared, but fresh reporting from Saints beat reporter Nick Underhill says he is not expected to have a huge role even if active against Detroit. New Orleans is expected to ease him back while he completes the MCL return, so availability remains improved but the Week 1 workload multiplier is reduced from the prior assumption.
Alvin Kamara.expectedReturn: Expected Week 1 if no setback; limited role anticipated

Isiah Pacheco.note: On injured reserve and must miss at least four games. Detroit has not provided a firm return timetable.

Tank Dell.note: On injured reserve with a knee issue and unavailable until at least Week 5.

James Conner.note: On injured reserve with a foot injury and unavailable for the opening portion of the season.

Jeremiyah Love.status: Expected active Week 1 - high ankle sprain; reduced workload possible
Jeremiyah Love.note: ESPN now reports that Love is expected to play Sunday against the Chargers after battling the high-ankle sprain since mid-August. That is a meaningful upgrade from the prior game-time-decision outlook. Availability is raised close to full, while a modest workload penalty remains because of the recent high-ankle sprain and Arizona's planned backfield rotation.
Jeremiyah Love.expectedReturn: Expected active Week 1; reduced workload possible

Josh Jacobs.note: Currently unavailable to play because of an off-field league status with no established football return date. This adjustment reflects availability uncertainty, not injury performance risk.

Brock Bowers.note: Las Vegas has officially ruled Bowers out for Week 1 after his meniscus trim. Current reporting continues to estimate a one-to-two-game absence, and the Raiders have not announced a longer timetable. The multipliers are unchanged because the prior adjustment already assumed he would miss the opener and potentially an additional game; the final designation removes remaining Week 1 uncertainty without materially changing the expected recovery window.

Malik Nabers.status: Questionable Week 1 - ACL/meniscus return; Giants add WR insurance
Malik Nabers.note: Nabers practiced fully all week but remains questionable and has not committed to playing Sunday night. On Saturday, New York elevated Braxton Berrios and added Dalen Cambre to the active roster, giving the Giants extra wide-receiver insurance while Nabers' status remains unresolved. The moves do not officially rule him out, but they increase the probability that he is inactive or limited compared with the prior outlook, so short-term availability and workload assumptions are reduced while long-term post-ACL/meniscus risk is unchanged.
Malik Nabers.expectedReturn: Week 1 game-time decision; limited role possible if active

Xavier Legette.note: Not listed on Carolina's Week 1 injury report after recovering from the August ankle injury and walking-boot period. He is medically cleared for the opener; any playing-time limitation is role-based rather than injury-based.

Jakobi Meyers.note: Jacksonville gave Meyers no final game designation after three limited practices with the thumb injury. He is cleared to play against Cleveland. A very small workload cushion remains because he practiced in a non-contact jersey earlier in the week and the injury involves his catching hand, but the prior availability concern is removed.

Marvin Mims Jr..status: Cleared Week 1 - foot; no game designation
Marvin Mims Jr..note: Denver's final Saturday injury report listed Mims as a full participant for the third straight practice and assigned him no game status. The Broncos said all 53 players are expected to be available Monday night against Kansas City, so the temporary workload cushion tied to the foot issue is removed.
Marvin Mims Jr..expectedReturn: Active Week 1; no injury limitation expected

Patrick Mahomes.note: Fully cleared following ACL/LCL rehabilitation and expected to start Week 1. Mahomes has reported no planned playing restrictions; only a minimal residual long-term post-reconstruction risk modifier remains until regular-season game action is confirmed.

A.J. Brown.note: New England has now placed Brown on injured reserve after the high-ankle sprain suffered in the opener. He must miss at least the next four games, and current reporting places the recovery window at roughly four to six weeks. The multipliers are unchanged because the prior adjustment had already priced in an expected absence of at least four weeks; the IR move increases certainty around that timeline rather than materially worsening the projected recovery.
A.J. Brown.expectedReturn: Earliest Week 6; approximately 4-6 week recovery window

Sam Darnold.status: OUT Week 2 - hip strain; no structural damage
Sam Darnold.note: Follow-up testing showed no structural damage after the right hip injury suffered in Seattle's opener. The injury is muscular rather than a fracture or major structural issue. Darnold is expected to miss Week 2, with a possible return in Week 3 if his recovery progresses normally.

Alec Pierce.status: Cleared Week 1 - heel surgery recovery; snap count TBD
Alec Pierce.note: Pierce has no Week 1 game designation and is cleared to play after heel surgery, but ESPN Colts reporter Stephen Holder reported that his snap count is still to be determined. Because Pierce only returned to practice on Sept. 1 and was limited throughout game week, a full complement of snaps is not expected. Availability remains fully restored, while the workload multiplier is reduced to reflect a likely managed return.
Alec Pierce.expectedReturn: Active Week 1; reduced snap count possible

Jacory Croskey-Merritt.note: Washington says its full 53-man roster is medically cleared for Week 1, including Croskey-Merritt after he was limited Wednesday and Thursday with the groin injury. A modest workload cushion remains because the team indicated snap-count decisions could still be discussed for players returning from injuries, but he no longer carries a meaningful availability penalty.

De'Zhaun Stribling.status: OUT Week 1 - left ankle; severity pending
De'Zhaun Stribling.note: Suffered a non-contact left-ankle injury in the second quarter of San Francisco's opener after briefly returning from an earlier ankle issue. He could not bear full weight and was carted off. Kyle Shanahan said the Achilles is intact, but the magnitude of the ankle injury remains unknown and further evaluation is pending.

Sean Tucker.status: Doubtful Week 1 - hamstring; Bucs elevate RB insurance
Sean Tucker.note: Tampa Bay already listed Tucker doubtful after the hamstring issue limited him throughout game week. On Saturday the Buccaneers elevated RB Josh Williams from the practice squad, with the team's official site explicitly citing Tucker's doubtful status and the risk of entering the game with only two healthy active-roster backs. That move further increases the expectation Tucker will be inactive, so his short-term availability and workload multipliers are reduced while long-term risk remains minimal.
Sean Tucker.expectedReturn: Week 2 possible if held out Week 1

Jalen McMillan.note: Tampa Bay listed McMillan doubtful for the opener despite a full Friday practice while returning from a knee issue that limited him earlier in the week. The doubtful designation makes a Week 1 absence likely, while the full practice keeps the expected return window relatively short if there is no setback.
